input.voiceNotes: Okay, flat above the dry cleaner's on Streatham High Road, well, maisonette, first and second floor, own front door round the back off the service yard, you share the yard with the shop for bins. Two beds, second's small, vendor calls it a double, it's two-seven by two-four so it's a single. Living room's big, bay onto the High Road, bit of traffic noise obviously. Kitchen's 2022. Bathroom top floor. Lease eighty-nine left, solicitor's served the section 42, buyer can take it over. Ground rent three-fifty, doubles every twenty-five, next one 2034. Service charge about nine-sixty, includes buildings insurance. Shop owner's the freeholder. OIEO three-seven-five. Station six minutes, Common ten. Gas combi. Basically a three-bed if you do the loft. Don't put that in, there's no permission.

input.voiceNotes: Right, Oak Lane, Sevenoaks. 1930s semi, big rear extension 2021, kitchen-family room, bifolds, island, Quooker. Loft conversion 2019 with en-suite, building regs signed off, I've seen the completion cert. Four beds, three baths counting the en-suite, family bathroom and the ground-floor shower room. Original stained glass in the front door and hall window. Log burner in the sitting room. Garden south-west, about a hundred foot, garden office at the end with power. Drive for two, garage converted to utility and shower room. Station point eight of a mile, London Bridge about twenty-five. It's in the Sevenoaks School and grammar annexe area, families love it, careful how you word that. Guide nine-seven-five. They've found somewhere so there's a chain.

input.voiceNotes: Right so Brook Hall, outside Frant, about four miles from Tunbridge Wells. Detached Edwardian, 1908 on the datestone, tile-hung, five beds, four baths. Gated drive, about four and a half acres all in including a three-acre paddock. Outdoor pool heated off an air source, and the oak-framed triple cart lodge, permission last year, it's built. Annexe over it, one bed, the mum lived there, not sure if it's separately banded, TBC. Honestly best view in the High Weald, absolutely stunning, write that. Oil in the main house, treatment plant 2022. Public footpath across the bottom of the paddock. High Weald National Landscape. Frant station two miles, London Bridge about an hour. Guide two-point-one. Mobile's patchy indoors.

input.voiceNotes: So, Forge Cottages, Smarden, number two, end of terrace, Victorian, about 1880, red brick, clay tiles. Two beds, bathroom upstairs. Cast-iron fireplace in the sitting room, vendor says original, I can't swear to it, so just cast-iron fireplace. Quarry tiles in the kitchen, beams are reclaimed, nineties, not original. Ledged and braced doors throughout. There's a range alcove, it is NOT an inglenook. Low ceiling at the top of the stairs, about six-two, mention it. Cottage garden about forty foot, brick path, shed. Septic tank shared with number one, it's in their garden, emptied yearly, split the cost, vendor doesn't know if it meets the 2020 rules, so say that. Bottom of the garden's flood zone two on the EA map, house never flooded. Conservation area. Oil heating. On-street parking. Guide four-two-five. Lovely chocolate-box village, pub's two minutes.

input.voiceNotes: Right, new build, Plot 47 Orchard Rise, Kings Hill, the Larch, three-bed semi, completes spring 2027. Fixed price four-ten. Reservation fee fifteen hundred, comes off the price at completion, refundable less two-fifty admin if they pull out within twenty-eight days, otherwise not. Freehold but there's an estate charge, two-nine-five a year to the management company for the open space. EPC predicted B off the SAP, so say predicted. Council tax not banded yet. Ten-year NHBC. Air source, underfloor downstairs, EV charger, two allocated spaces. Photos are the show home, plot 12, and the outside's a CGI. Developer's doing five grand towards flooring, ends 30 November. Only three Larches left, push that, get them in.
